name: Puerto Rico

findings.controller: Covered-list manufacturer (Huawei and/or ZTE; not named in filings)
findings.local_actor: Puerto Rico Telephone Company, Inc. (PRTC, d/b/a Claro Puerto Rico); US Federal Communications Commission (Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program)
findings.financier: US FCC Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program
findings.reversal_of: PRTC's covered communications equipment: stored fixed-network gear plus about 39,000 wireless routers, USB modems and hotspots, many loaned to customers after Hurricane Maria
findings.summary: In FCC rip-and-replace filings, PRTC reports replacing and destroying its covered fixed-network equipment (January 2023), destroying all spare wireless units, and recovering about 69% of customer-loaned units by April 2025, cancelling service for non-returners.
findings.analyst_inference: The filings say only 'covered communications equipment'; the reimbursement programme covers Huawei and ZTE equipment, so pole prc is inferred from programme scope, not a named vendor. Reversal reason geopolitical (Secure Networks Act national-security exclusion), consistent with ASM-002. All three sources are the same filer's self-reports, so not independent; medium because S1. Tier 5: deployed at scale before removal. Replacement vendors unnamed. Completion not confirmed: PRTC sought a deadline extension in February 2025 and expects not to recover remaining loaned units.

findings.summary: Liberty Latin America expanded 5G in Puerto Rico with an Ericsson-supplied 5G mobile core and IP stack, reported as operational in August 2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Ericsson supplies the core, so pole third. Only the article's lead was readable (paywall); RAN vendor not stated. Single source, so low. Liberty Latin America is US-listed but Ericsson, as equipment vendor, sets the pole.

findings.local_actor: Puerto Rico Police Bureau (Department of Public Safety)
findings.summary: The Puerto Rico Police Bureau equipped officers across the territory with Axon Body 4 cameras managed through Axon Evidence, extending an earlier rollout of Axon Body 3 and Fleet 3 in-car cameras.
findings.analyst_inference: Axon is the vendor operating the evidence-management system, so pole us. All three trade-press items appear to relay one Axon announcement, so treated as not independent and not corroborated. No AI features are described; relevance to the AI stack is as a US-controlled police data platform. Camera count and contract value not stated.
